sol.fix: Change borrow.rs::validate_borrow_frames and claims.rs::borrow_frames_certified/check_borrow_independence. §4.3 says qreturn is the "matched inverse of qborrow after its frame"; §5.1 requires "every qborrow by a qreturn after its frame"; §5.6 requires the FRAME to satisfy "P_F = P′ ⊗ I_B". A proof of the final whole-region map on a physically reused pool is not a proof of every completed frame. Distinguish a definite violated lifetime/non-permutation rule from a symbolic identity the checker cannot decide: never let a certificate suppress the former. The library route for undecidable identities must establish the actual named frames/lifetimes, independently of future borrowing or whole-loop cancellation. Add the exact X and CX fixtures above to tests/r1_certificates.rs and r1_borrow.rs with both absent and present certificates; all must fail Object::parse and hash/check with §5.6, exit 1 and empty stdout. Construct these certificate bindings from the independently computed envelopes, rather than requiring the invalid uncertified object to parse. Keep valid carried borrowing across an even loop and doubled-X/doubled-CX per-lifetime positives accepted, including entangled borrowed references. No budget is involved.

sol.problem:
The new generic-body Return proof discards known-clean loop-entry workspace and rejects a valid identity. Use the same memoryless ptr_width=32 perm_action signature mut=[1], in=[], mem=[], args=[], bounds=[2], header/regs as B01, with body:
^entry():
d = qalloc any 1
qloop 2 {
b = qborrow any 1
cx d b
qreturn b
}
qfree d
Reproduced hash /dev/stdin: exit 1, empty stdout, "§5.6: qreturn does not restore borrowed wire v2_0". The equivalent unrolled two borrow/CX/return lifetimes are accepted (interface hash 8c8594f020bbb1986a0586e6774e8a889b06e71dd4e3136fb8e202a8a97f76f8). Hand: d is allocated as |0>, never written, and every CX is exactly identity, so EACH arbitrary, possibly entangled borrowed b is restored and no output depends on it. Repeat collects the entry substitution d=0 but replaces state with independent identity variables before checking Return; the necessary substitution is applied only after the erroneous rejection. The previous snapshot's boundary-free Repeat squares this two-CX map to identity and accepts this exact case, so this is also a regression introduced while fixing the unsafe loop-local lifetime cases.
sol.fix: Change borrow.rs::Evaluation::apply for Repeat and its lifetime-obligation representation. §4.3 specifies "n clean wires" for qalloc; §5.2's domain says "qalloc'ed wires at 0"; §14.2 says "qalloc tensors |0⟩"; §4.6 says "body n times". Prove every internal return on its reachable loop-entry state, retaining known-zero and other established invariants of surrounding live wires, while keeping each new borrowed entry independent. Do not require a return to hold for arbitrary values of wires already proven clean, and do not reinstate the old aggregate-parity acceptance. Add the exact positive above to tests/r1_borrow.rs with trip counts 1,2,3 and a large bound plus nesting; parser/hash/check must accept, run-action must preserve t=0/1 and superpositions, and forward/adjoint must preserve b entangled with an untouched reference. Its alpha-renamed unrolling must agree. Negative control: X d before the loop (and X d after for explicit d cleanup) must still reject each one-CX borrowed lifetime, even at an even bound. No certificate or execution budget is needed.

sol.problem:
Runtime workspace widths are keyed by bare spelling across different consumed lifetimes. Exact memoryless ptr_width=32 signature {"abi":"0.8","args":[],"bounds":[],"in":[],"kind":"perm_action","mem":[],"mut":[1],"tier":"q"}; body:
perm_action @a (t:wire mut) () () () ()
^entry():
d = qalloc any 1
cx t d
cx t d
qfree d
d = qalloc any 2
qfree d
hash gives interface/closure ba05b26390994f78dc6405906f8ecf555075f83b6f2c47da1ffbee78e7afd140. After substitution, check succeeds with object_hash 1004ce41faf18591bbfa75d3cff461a2c61c0df9f3a89bcac513b3553c223340. run-action /dev/stdin a --mut 1 and reverse both exit 1, empty stdout, "§3.3: scalar wire required". Hand: the first d is one clean wire, two CX gates cancel, it is freed; the second d is two different clean wires and is freed. This is identity on t. infer_widths scans the entire function and overwrites widths["d"] with 2; the first qalloc then uses that final width rather than its own literal 1. Alpha-renaming only the second lifetime to e makes execution and reversal succeed (state {"1":[1,0]}, equals_entry=true).
sol.fix: Change action.rs::infer_widths, Environment::widths and action_sequence to track widths per producing/consuming lifetime or instruction identity, including reverse traversal; forward qalloc/qborrow must allocate their own declared width, and inverse release must recover the width of the matching producer. §4.3 defines qalloc as "n clean wires"; §5.1 requires each allocation's explicit matched cleanup; §5.3's adjoint table explicitly has "versions renumbered". A later definition cannot resize a previously consumed value. Add this exact fixture to tests/quantum.rs and tests/cli_xam.rs: check and forward/adjoint execution for mut=0 and 1 must succeed with unchanged t and no workspace; reverse must report equals_entry=true. Cover superposition and reused names from qcopy/qload/qborrow, including different widths in nested structured code and inverse traversal. Retain rejection of producing a name while its prior lifetime is still live. No budget is needed.

sol.problem: The public sparse amplitude observer reports the unnormalised projection instead of the conditional state. Reproduced with a temporary read-only-library harness: let mut q=QuantumState::new(); let w=q.allocate(2).unwrap(); q.gate("h", &[w[0]], None, &[]).unwrap(); let branches=q.measurement_branches(&[w[0]]).unwrap(); For BOTH outcomes, probability=0.5 and branch.state.amplitudes() is [Complex{re:1,im:0}, Complex{re:0,im:0}], but branch.state.exact_support() is [([false], (0.7071067811865476,0))]. Hand: H on the first wire gives (|00>+|10>)/sqrt(2) in wire-order spelling; either measurement leaves the untouched wire in |0> with amplitude 1. The reported sparse vector has squared norm 1/2, although the dense observer correctly gives norm 1. measurement_branches deliberately retains unnormalised exact shadows for later Born ratios; exact_support evaluates those raw shadows without compensating for their common normalization. This pre-existing issue remains visible after the new measurement work; it is not a claim that tiny-outcome selection is still wrong.
sol.fix: Change quantum.rs::exact_support and the normalization metadata of projected QuantumState values. §14.2 specifies "projective computational-basis measurement with Born probabilities": a MeasurementBranch.state must describe its conditional state, and both amplitude observers must report that same state. Retain unnormalised exact shadows for sound support/cleanliness and Born-ratio decisions, but retain their scale/projection marker and apply the appropriate normalization when emitting sparse amplitudes (using the refined extended-exponent evaluation where necessary). Do not silently normalize arbitrary set_state_vector input, whose API explicitly leaves normalization to its caller. Add the exact two-wire test above to tests/quantum.rs, checking sparse amplitude (1,0) and agreement with amplitudes() for each branch; after H on the surviving wire, both supported amplitudes must be 1/sqrt(2), with norm 1. Extend the existing tiny entangled-residual tests to check exact_support too, with finite normalized amplitudes and unchanged subsequent Born results. This is an output-contract fix, not a probability floor or change to measurement reversal eligibility.

action @a (t:wire mut) () () () ()

regs {  } bounds {1}
^entry():
c = qalloc any 1
b = qborrow any 1
qloop 1 {
qfree c
}
qreturn b
The independently computed interface hash is a42079194137127e703185faaeb6b5bc85c6941ccc03988eb67c19c14481e8df. check, run-action a --mut 1, and reverse a --mut 1 all exit 1, no stdout, with §5.6: a wire released inside a borrow frame is not clean.
